title: DNS Advanced
description: DNS resolution, delegation, and record hygiene.

attacks.name: DNS rebinding
attacks.desc: A hostname that changes from public to private IP can bypass controls that check DNS only once.
attacks.prevention: Resolve and recheck addresses after DNS changes, and block private or metadata destinations on every server-side request.

attacks.name: DNS tunneling
attacks.desc: DNS requests or records can carry data out of a network that permits resolver traffic.
attacks.prevention: Restrict DNS egress to trusted resolvers and monitor unusual high-volume or encoded query patterns.

attacks.name: Wildcard DNS abuse
attacks.desc: Wildcard records can make arbitrary subdomains resolve and may confuse host validation or tenant routing.
attacks.prevention: Validate Host against an explicit allowlist and do not treat wildcard DNS as proof of tenant ownership.

attacks.name: CNAME chain hijack
attacks.desc: A dangling target within a CNAME chain can allow another party to control the final destination.

attacks.name: Zone file leak
attacks.desc: An unauthorized AXFR response can reveal a DNS zone's hostnames and addresses.

attacks.name: DNS cache poisoning
attacks.desc: Forged DNS answers accepted by a resolver can redirect traffic to an unintended endpoint.

attacks.name: Subdomain enumeration via CT
attacks.desc: Certificate transparency logs can reveal subdomains from publicly recorded certificate names.

attacks.name: MX/SPF/DMARC gaps
attacks.desc: Missing or weak mail DNS records can reduce spoofing protection or misroute email.
